title: Don't Trust the Me Who's Talking
amb: quiet desk at night, laptop fan hum, faint rain on a window; on the line: dead concrete room, buzzing red emergency light, muffled pounding on a steel door

lines.text: Eleven twenty-four. Your laptop fan hums. Rain ticks against the window.
Your phone buzzes once. A voice memo from Lena. Four seconds long.
[whispering] Don't trust the me who's talking.
That's all. You've never seen her face. But you know this voice. You'd know it anywhere.
On your second screen, the Meridian building feed is open. A woman's voice comes through, bright and easy.
I'm fine. Everything's fine down here. Don't send anyone.
A paper cup scrapes across a desk. Short. Dry.
Under the feed sits an anonymous message. It came before any of this. Midnight. Gas. Six years ago, the same night.
The feed rolls on. Then you hear the same breath again, and the same little laugh.
I'm fine. Everything's fine down here. Don't send anyone.
The same scrape of the cup follows. It's word for word. Even the hiss underneath matches.
You open the direct line. It rings once.
[low] You got it. Good. Keep your voice down.
Her breathing is right against your ear. Behind her, a red light buzzes like a trapped insect.
I'm in the screening room. Sub-level two. The door's locked.
Power's dead. It locked about seven minutes ago. I didn't touch it.
You tell her the building feed is playing her voice. It keeps saying she's fine.
I heard it through the hall speaker. That's not me. What do you see on yours?
You tell her what you hear. The same sentence, played twice. Every sound is identical.
Then a bang. Steel shudders through the line. A second bang follows.
Someone is on the other side of her door.
Okay. Someone's out there. Those are fists. Nobody's knocking.
The pounding stops. The silence afterward is worse.
A cold thought settles in. The feed sounded like her too. So how do you know this one is real?
You tell her you need proof. It has to be something no recording could know.
[tense] Fair. Ask me. Fast.
You pick two words neither of you has ever said. Blue umbrella.
Her breath catches. Then she answers.
Blue umbrella. Want a knock too?
Two soft taps land right on the mic. They're live and close. It's her.
On your other screen, the feed is still cheerful. I'm fine. Scrape.
So. You believe me now?
Before you can answer, you hear something small and metal.
It's the door handle. Someone is turning it slowly from outside.
[whispering] The handle's moving. Someone's trying it.
There's a latch by the frame. Or I hide. Tell me which.
Eleven twenty-seven. The handle stops halfway. Then it holds there, waiting.

prompt: The handle is half-turned and someone is on the other side. Lena is waiting for you to tell her what to do right now.
choices: Lena, throw the latch now. Lean on it and don't make a sound.
Lena, leave the door. Get behind the projector, kill your light, and wait.
